notes: The San Francisco Call's daily Building Contracts list, printed in the Real Estate Transactions column, read for the whole of 1911 from curiv_betteravia_ver02 (January-August) and curiv_angwin_ver02 (September-December). The list ran most days, not weekly. Located by two passes over every page, one on the list's heading (which the OCR mangles: 'nnlldlnjc Contract*') and one heading-free on the entry's own shape ('with CONTRACTOR—WORK ... line/corner of ...; $AMOUNT'), merged into 286 page-blocks; each block read by hand into structured fields (contractor, work, storeys, material, use, side, street, offset, direction, cross street, lot, amount). A contract reprinted in a later issue is kept once, at its first printing (extra.reprinted lists the later dates). Replaces the two-entry January sample of 2026-09-27, whose entries named private owners. Private owners, trustees, estates and co-owners are cut from address_as_written, raw and extra; institutional and company owners are kept in extra.owner_firm, contractors and architects in extra.contractors and extra.architect. Every entry carries extra.record_date (1911 is after the 1909 renumbering). Placed with research/tools/corner.py --batch in its new dir mode, which measures each lot's frontage along the record's street from its crossing with the cross street, the way the record's compass direction runs: a placement needs a single parcel matching the roll year within two years and, where the record gives them, the offset within 4 ft and the lot area within 4%; its EAS point on the side of the street, or in the quadrant of the corner, the record names; a storey count within one and a half of the record's; and a parcel still on the current roll. Hand placements carry by_hand with the measurement in method. Where several contracts name the same building, the general contract (else the earliest) carries the page's entry and the others are declined as folded into it.

coverage.remaining: Nothing of the 1911 lists is known to remain unread. 90 entries match several parcels with nothing in the record to choose between them, and 75 single candidates were refused (the wrong side of the street for 58); a later run with a lot-line survey or a second source (the Edwards Abstract, the Building and Engineering News) could place some. The 1912 and 1913 lists are next: the 1912 batches are on the bulk route and 1913's are held only for February and July-December.
coverage.note: 8,897 OCR pages scanned; 286 page-blocks hold the list; 1,348 contract entries read, 1,341 findings after 7 reprints collapsed (1,186 building contracts, 155 alterations). 175 resolved - 167 by corner and offset with corner.py, 8 by a printed street number - and 1,166 unresolved: 699 whose corner or block face has no parcel matching the record's lot or offset with a roll year near 1911 (the building replaced, or the lot re-cut), 90 matching several parcels, 75 single candidates refused on side, storeys or a retired parcel, 89 whose streets could not be measured, and 213 with no cross street, a whole block, or no legible location. 152 published on 152 pages, 94 of them seeded; 23 declined - 19 folded into another contract for the same building, 4 repeating what the page carries or saying nothing a reader needs.
